openings.claim: Map disagreements to documented definition overlaps: ambiguity predicts boundary concentration; inconsistent application also predicts disagreements beyond boundaries.
openings.discriminator: Disagreement well outside overlaps weakens ambiguity-only; boundary clustering alone cannot exclude inconsistent application.
openings.probe: Proposed only: inspect current anonymous responses and record boundary mappings alongside preserved original labels.
openings.uncertainty: Boundary interpretation may vary. Neither account is established; stop short of attribution if mappings cannot support the distinction.

openings.claim: Independently recode the existing set: category ambiguity predicts recurring case-specific disagreement more strongly than arbitrary isolated application mistakes.
openings.discriminator: No recurrence weakens that directional prediction; unresolved coder independence defeats comparison. No guaranteed advantage over boundary auditing.
openings.probe: First establish independent coder availability and independence; only then recode current anonymous responses, preserving original decisions, and examine recurrence.
openings.uncertainty: Independent coders are indispensable; availability is unknown. Stop this comparison unless independence is established. No new responses are assumed.
